title: Jet Fuel Hits a Record High — and Holiday Plane Tickets Cost More
summary:
Planning to fly somewhere for the holidays? Your ticket will probably cost more this year — a lot more.

The reason is jet fuel, the special fuel airplanes burn. It is one of the biggest costs airlines have, and its price just hit a record. On Thursday, the average price of jet fuel in the United States reached $4.90 a gallon, according to the tracking firm Argus. That is the highest one-day average the firm has ever recorded — and more than twice what it cost a year ago.

Airlines are passing part of that cost on to passengers. “Airfares right now are at what we see as a 10-year high because of the high cost of jet fuel,” said Hayley Berg, the lead economist at Hopper, a travel company. Tickets for Thanksgiving trips are up about 30% compared with last year, she said, and Christmas tickets are up more than 20%.

Surprisingly, people are still buying. Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian said travelers have shown only a “limited amount of resistance” and still see flying as reasonably affordable. Berg says holiday travel is “sticky”: families really want to get home or take their big trip, so most are not canceling.

Airlines say they are absorbing most of the extra fuel cost themselves and passing only some of it to customers. Even so, some travelers are changing plans. One Maryland traveler said tickets for her whole family cost too much, so she will drive to Chicago instead.

And the shoppers who are flying are hunting for deals: Berg says many people booked their holiday trips earlier than usual this year, hoping to lock in a fare before prices climb even higher.
why_it_matters: Fuel is one of the biggest costs of flying, so when its price jumps, holiday trips and family visits become more expensive for everyone. Even so, most travelers are still booking, which shows how much people value getting home for the holidays.

background_read: Jet fuel is the special fuel that jet airplanes burn, and buying it is one of the biggest costs an airline has.
When fuel gets more expensive, airlines often raise ticket prices, because they pass part of the extra cost on to passengers.
The end of the year is one of the busiest times to fly, as families travel for Thanksgiving and Christmas.
Because so many people want to fly at the same time, holiday tickets are often among the most expensive of the year.
